# .agents/ — how agent work is kept in {{project}}

Every kind of fact has one home. Write a fact in its home and link to it from anywhere else; never copy it.
`aw doctor` checks all of this in one run. `aw <command> --help` documents each command.

| Fact | Home | Budget | Check |
|---|---|---|---|
| What is where | root `AGENTS.md`; a hub `AGENTS.md` in every non-leaf code directory | 200 / 40 lines | `aw hubs` |
| Project rules | root `AGENTS.md` § Rules, with a link to the why | 5 lines each | `aw dup` |
| Why, measurements, lessons | `.agents/memory/<folder>/<date>-<slug>.md` | 400 lines, 12 a folder | `aw memory lint` |
| Status | the one memory of type `status` | 120 lines | `aw memory lint` |
| What is done | the git log and closed cards | derived | `aw status` |
| Decisions | `.agents/decisions/NNNN-slug.md` | 150 lines | `aw decisions lint` |
| Words | `.agents/CONTEXT.md` | 300 characters a row | `aw decisions lint` |
| Protocols, formats, how to extend | `.agents/contracts/` | | `aw links` |
| Plans and specs | `.agents/plan/` | | the planning tool's own |
| Tasks and their status | cards in `.agents/kanban/` of the main working tree | | `aw kanban lint` |
| Checks still owed | cards of kind `gate` | | `aw kanban lint` |
| Briefs | `.agents/briefs/common.md`, `.agents/briefs/rounds/<date>-<slug>.md` | 120 / 80 lines | `aw doctor` |
| Reports | the final message, the pull request, the card | never a file | |
| Settings of these tools | `.agents/agent-works.json` | | `aw doctor` |
| Documentation for users | `docs/`, and nothing agent-facing goes there | | `aw doctor` |
| True on any project of this machine | shared learnings | | `aw learn search` |

Never: status or a changelog in `AGENTS.md`; a Done list in the status memory; a report saved as a file; a task
list in prose; a hand edit of a generated file (this page, a generated `INDEX.md`, the decisions `README.md`, a `CLAUDE.md`
twin).

## Orientation

Read the root `AGENTS.md`, then the hub of the folder you work in. A hub lists its direct children, one line each:
what the child holds and when to open it. A directory with a hub holds no source files; a directory that holds
source files has no hub. When you add, move, rename or repurpose something, fix its parent's hub in that change.
`CLAUDE.md` beside an `AGENTS.md` is its one-line twin, written by `aw twins`.

## Memory

- Read first: `.agents/memory/INDEX.md`, the status memory, then the indexes and memories your task touches. A
  memory is a claim as of its date: check what it names against the code, and fix the memory when the code differs.
- One topic per file. Frontmatter: `name` (the slug: unique, permanent), `description` (the index line: what is in
  the file and when it matters), `type` (`status`, `decision`, `learning`, `report`, `reference`), `updated`.
- New: `aw memory new <folder> <slug> --type <type> --description "<line>"`. Changed: `aw memory touch <slug>`
  (date, file name, links, its folder's index). Link another memory as `[[slug]]`.
- An `INDEX.md` whose second line says `generated by aw memory index` is generated: change a memory's
  `description`, not the list. One without that line is hand-written: the two commands change one line of it and
  leave the rest; `aw memory index --adopt` converts it, once the descriptions say what its lines said.
- Update the memory that covers a topic instead of adding a second. Delete what turned out wrong.
- The status memory holds Goal, Current focus and Known issues, the last two as links to cards. Nothing else.
- Not memory: what the code or git already says, tasks, rules, session narratives, secrets.
- A lesson about the machine or a tool, not about this project: `aw learn add` shares it with every project here.

## Decisions and words

- A choice that is hard to reverse, surprising without context, or a real trade-off gets a record:
  `aw decisions new "<title>"` (Status, Sources, Context, Decision, Consequences).
- A record takes one amendment. When the choice changes, a new record supersedes it.
- A new term goes into the glossary in the change that introduces it. One word per thing, everywhere.

## Tasks

- Something worth doing that is outside your change: a card. `aw kanban add "<title>" --suggest --details "<what
  you saw, why it matters, where to look, what done looks like>"`. Then carry on.
- A card handed to you: do it, then `aw kanban move <id> review`. The owner moves it to done.
- A check you cannot run now (it needs another checkout, a free machine, the owner): `aw kanban owe "<the check>"
  --ref <what it is owed for> --needs "<what running it needs>"`. Once it ran and passed:
  `aw kanban settle <id> --evidence "<the command and what it showed>"`. An owed check is never skipped silently.
- Where the project stands: `aw status` (the board, owed gates, locks, claims, the last merges).

## Working beside other agents

- One task, one branch, one worktree per agent. Stage files by their exact paths; commit as you go.
- Branch, commit, push, open the pull request and merge it when its gates are green, without asking for
  approval. A step is held for the owner only where the owner asked for that (in the task, or a rule in the root
  `AGENTS.md`). A forced push is always the owner's.
- An application or device of which one runs at a time is a lock: `aw lock run <resource> --for "<what, how long>"
  -- <command>`. Exit 3 with `STILL QUEUED` means you do not hold it: run the same command again.
- Heavy shared use is a lease: `aw lease gpu --share 0.5 --mem 12GB --for "<what>" -- <command>`.
- Before timing anything: `aw sys --quiet-for timing --wait 120`, and keep the `record:` line of `aw sys` beside
  the numbers.
- A number several branches bump (a schema or format version): `aw claim <counter>` when you are about to merge.
- What others must know now, in one line: `aw note "<text>"`. Read theirs: `aw notes`. Who is running: `aw who`.

## The guard

`.agents/agent-works.json` turns on a hook that refuses staging the whole tree, staging or editing the owner's own
files, hand edits of generated files, starting a locked resource without its lock, and an expensive run without
its stated reason. A refusal says what to do instead. It is there for mistakes that already happened once: do
what it says rather than rephrasing the command.
